notes:
VINTAGE: WHO GHE 2021 (released 2024) is STILL the latest GHE vintage as of Aug 2026; next release expected ~2027-28. IHME has published the GBD 2023 capstone (Global burden of 292 causes of death, 1990-2023, healthdata.org), making GBD 2023 the newest overall vintage, but GBD 2021 remains the latest with widely citable per-cause secondary literature; nothing I could extract from GBD 2023 changes any verdict here. Disease-specific annual reports are newer than GHE and were preferred where they exist: Global TB Report 2025 (year 2024), World Malaria Report 2025 (year 2024), UNAIDS 2025 (year 2024), GLOBOCAN 2022 (cancers).

CORRECTIONS (2): pertussis 160,000 -> 59,000 (repo value is the 2014-era Yeung/WHO estimate of 160,700 under-5 deaths; GBD 2021 under-20 deaths = 51,517, all-ages ~59,000; COVID-era mask/distancing effects contributed to the drop, so expect some rebound in GBD 2023 given the 2024 case surge of ~941,565 reported cases). rotavirus 200,000 -> 128,500 (WHO-cited GBD figure for under-5 deaths, 2016; repo value is the pre-2016 estimate).

FLAGS (4): (a) sepsis: 11M (GBD 2017, Rudd 2020) is the standard WHO-cited figure, but sepsis deaths are 'sepsis-ASSOCIATED' and overlap with underlying causes (pneumonia, cancers, IHD) - summing it with other rows double-counts; the GBD 2021 update (Lancet Glob Health 2025) estimates 21.4M for 2021 inflated by COVID. Keep 11M only with a methodology disclosure. (b) covid-19: repo 1.2M matches no vintage - GHE 2021 says 8.8M (2021), WHO-reported deaths were ~0.25-0.32M in 2023 and tens of thousands/yr in 2024-25 (reporting largely ceased); the field needs an explicit year label; writing 8.8M unlabeled would also mislead. (c) ebola: deaths are episodic, not annual - 2024 = 0, 2025 = 32, but 2014-16 averaged ~3,800/yr; a flat 300/yr fabricates a steady state. Suggest showing most-recent-year with an 'epidemic-prone' note. (d) west-nile-virus: no global authority; CDC US mean ~130/yr; repo 200 is a plausible global order of magnitude but uncitable as stated.

METHODOLOGY-PAGE DISCLOSURES (framing that can mislead): sepsis double-counting (above) is the big one. Also: 'pneumonia' figure is WHO's 'lower respiratory infections' (includes flu, RSV, bronchiolitis); rotavirus and norovirus deaths are subsets of overall diarrhoeal-disease deaths (do not sum with a diarrhoea row); 'heart-disease' = ischaemic heart disease only (not all cardiovascular, which is ~19-20M); 'alzheimers-disease' = Alzheimer's AND other dementias; 'type-2-diabetes' = all diabetes direct deaths (excludes ~0.5M diabetes-attributed kidney deaths); breast/lung cancer use GLOBOCAN 2022 while others use GHE/GBD 2021 - mixed vintages should be stated. On paper-count vs deaths framing specifically: diseases with huge research footprints but modest current mortality (covid-19, ebola, cystic-fibrosis, west-nile-virus) will look 'over-studied' vs deaths, while sepsis looks 'under-studied' only because its 11M deaths overlap other categories - a scatter of publications vs mortality should disclose both the overlap and the year-labeling caveats.
